Band.description:
A pointwise band around the fitted curve at the requested ``x`` values.

``extrapolated[i]`` is true where ``x[i]`` lies outside the range of the active
(weight > 0) fitted points, where the band relies on the model form alone.
Band.title: Band

file.description: csv, tsv, txt, json or xlsx table
file.title: File

CrossValidation.description:
Outcome of one cross-validation run; ``None`` means a statistic is not defined.

``fold_rmse`` holds the weighted held-out RMSE of each fold in fold order, with
``None`` for a failed fold. ``rmse`` pools all held-out points and is ``None`` unless
every fold succeeded. ``n_failed`` counts failed folds and ``reasons`` names each one,
so no fold is silently dropped or replaced. ``status`` is ``"ok"`` only when no fold
failed. Note that ``"ok"`` means the estimate is complete, not that the model is valid:
cross-validation quantifies predictive accuracy, it does not confirm the model.
CrossValidation.title: CrossValidation

CurveSamples.description: The fitted curve sampled at ``CURVE_POINTS`` x values; every ``y`` is finite.
CurveSamples.title: CurveSamples

CustomRef.description:
A user equation: ``equation`` is ``y = <expression>`` or just the right-hand side.

``parameters`` are the names to fit; ``variable`` is the independent variable. The text
is checked by the safe expression grammar and is never evaluated as Python.
CustomRef.title: CustomRef

DataSnapshot.description:
The fit input a bundle was computed from, so a bundle stands on its own.

``n_total`` is the number of rows the fit used. With ``subsampled`` the arrays hold an
evenly strided subset (first and last row included) and are for plotting only.
DataSnapshot.title: DataSnapshot

DiagnosticTest.description:
One statistical test applied to the residuals of a fit.

``statistic``, ``p_value`` and ``df`` are ``None`` when the test does not produce them:
a test that does not apply, or a statistic-only test such as the Durbin-Watson.
``status`` is ``"ok"`` when the test was computed and ``"not_applicable"`` when the
data cannot support it; ``reason`` then says why.  ``reason`` may also carry a note on
how a test was computed (a clamped lag, for instance) while ``status`` is ``"ok"``.

``null_hypothesis`` states what the test assumes, ``assumptions`` what it needs for
the result to mean anything and ``limitations`` what it cannot show.  ``note`` is the
same on every result.
DiagnosticTest.title: DiagnosticTest

DiagnosticsReport.description: The tests run on one fit, in the order they were run.
DiagnosticsReport.title: DiagnosticsReport

FitBundle.description:
One fit with everything a UI or report needs.

``result.status`` says whether the fit converged. When it did not (or a quantity is not
defined) the matching field is ``None`` and the ``*_reason`` field says why; a curve is
never substituted for a failed fit. ``summary`` is the ``describe_fit`` report
(information criteria, residual diagnostics, tests); ``curve`` covers the data range
extended by 5 % each side; the bands are pointwise at the curve's x values.
FitBundle.title: FitBundle

FitReport.description:
Everything :func:`describe_fit` computed for one converged fit.

``result_summary`` holds ``model_id`` and ``status`` (strings) and ``n``, ``k``, ``df``,
``rmse`` plus, where defined, ``r2`` and ``adj_r2`` (numbers). A statistic that is not
defined is left out of the mapping, never stored as ``0.0`` or NaN. ``cv`` is ``None``
when no ``fitter`` was supplied. ``warnings`` merges the fit's own warnings with what the
bundle found: incomplete cross-validation, tests that did not apply and flagged points.

Like :class:`~curvestudio.fitting.FitResult` the model is frozen but its lists are not
deep-frozen; :meth:`to_json` re-checks finiteness, so a mutation that sneaks in NaN/inf
fails loudly instead of writing a file that cannot be read back.
FitReport.title: FitReport

FitResult.description:
Complete, immutable record of one fit.

The model is frozen, but list/dict fields are not deep-frozen: do not mutate them.
:meth:`to_json` re-checks finiteness, so a mutation that sneaks in NaN/inf fails
loudly rather than producing a file that cannot be read back.
FitResult.title: FitResult

FitSpec.description:
What to fit and how.

``bounds`` maps a parameter to ``(lower, upper)``; ``None`` means unbounded on that side
(JSON has no infinity). ``initial`` overrides the starting value per parameter; a custom
equation starts every parameter at 1.0 unless told otherwise. ``use_weights`` weights
the fit by the data's weights column (an error if the data has none); with ``False``
any weights in the data are ignored and a warning says so. ``seed`` (default 0) is
recorded in the result. ``time_limit`` is a wall-clock budget in seconds for
registered and custom models; a fit that exceeds it is reported ``failed``.

Polynomials are fitted in closed form, so ``method``, ``loss``, ``bounds`` and ``initial``
must be left at their defaults for them.
FitSpec.title: FitSpec

FitStatistics.description:
Goodness-of-fit summary. ``None`` means "not defined", never "not computed".

``n`` is the number of observations passed in; the engines pass the active
(weight > 0) points only, so zero-weight points are excluded from ``n`` and from
``df = n - k`` in every fit result.
FitStatistics.title: FitStatistics

FitStatus.description: Outcome category. A failed fit is reported as such, never as a plausible result.
FitStatus.title: FitStatus

InformationCriteria.description:
AIC, AICc and BIC of one converged fit under the shared Gaussian convention.

``k_total`` is ``k' = k + 1``: the fitted parameters plus the error variance.
``aicc`` is ``None`` when ``n - k' - 1 <= 0``, because the small-sample correction is
undefined there (it would divide by zero or turn negative), not because the fit failed.
``convention`` records the exact formulas so a stored result stays self-describing.
InformationCriteria.title: InformationCriteria

ModelInfo.description: What a UI needs to offer a model: identity, equation and parameters.
ModelInfo.title: ModelInfo

ParameterEstimate.description: One fitted parameter. ``None`` uncertainty means it could not be determined.
ParameterEstimate.title: ParameterEstimate

ParameterInfo.description: A model parameter; ``None`` bounds mean unbounded on that side.
ParameterInfo.title: ParameterInfo

PointsOut.description: Stride-sampled points; ``w`` is ``None`` when the dataset has no weights.
PointsOut.title: PointsOut

PolynomialRef.description: ``y = b0 + b1*x + ... + b<degree>*x**degree``, fitted by linear least squares.
PolynomialRef.title: PolynomialRef

Prediction.description:
Predicted values at the requested ``x`` (same order and length).

A row is ``None`` where it is undefined: a non-finite ``x``, or a model that has no
real value there. ``lower``/``upper`` are ``None`` when no band was requested or the
band is undefined altogether (``band_reason`` says why); individual rows may be ``None``.
``extrapolated[i]`` is true where ``x[i]`` lies outside the fitted data's range.
Prediction.title: Prediction

Provenance.description: What produced a result: software versions, input data identity, time and seed.
Provenance.title: Provenance

RegisteredRef.description: A model from the registry, by id (see :func:`curvestudio.workflow.list_models`).
RegisteredRef.title: RegisteredRef

ResidualSet.description:
Per-point residual diagnostics and plot-ready series for one fit.

Per-point lists (``x`` to ``scale_location``) hold the active points in input order and
have equal length. ``standardized``, ``studentized_external``, ``cooks_distance`` and
``scale_location`` are ``None`` where undefined (leverage-one points, a zero residual
variance, or too few degrees of freedom). ``qq_theoretical``/``qq_ordered`` pair the
normal quantiles at the Blom positions ``(i - 0.375)/(n + 0.25)`` with the sorted
weighted residuals. ``hist_edges``/``hist_counts`` histogram the weighted residuals
(Freedman-Diaconis bins, Sturges when the IQR is 0, or ``bins`` equal bins).

``acf`` is the demeaned, biased autocorrelation of the weighted residuals taken in
ascending-x order (ties keep input order) at lags ``0..nlags``; it is empty when the
residuals have no variance. ``acf_bound`` is ``1.96/sqrt(n)``. ``flagged_high_leverage``
(``h > 2k/n``) and ``flagged_high_influence`` (Cook's ``> 4/n``) index the active arrays;
leverage-one points are in both.
ResidualSet.title: ResidualSet

post.description: Revoke the refresh token (and anything rotated from it). Always 204: it reveals nothing.

Exchange a refresh token for a new pair; the old one is revoked.

Presenting a token that was already used (or revoked) means it leaked: the whole chain
of tokens descended from it is revoked and the request fails with 401.

Delete the account and everything in it.

audit trail is kept but anonymised: ``audit_logs.user_id`` is set to NULL, the one change
the append-only trigger allows. A final ``user.delete`` row records that it happened.
